title: Integral constructible complexes are normalized constructible towers
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$, and a scheme $T$ on which $\ell$ is invertible [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension, def-pc-scheme]. On the small pro-etale site of $T$ use the completed coefficient sheaf $R_T=\widehat{\mathcal O}_{E,T}=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$ [def-weil-completed-integral-coefficients, def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Write $D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)=D(\operatorname{Mod}(R_T))$ for its derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Use the coefficient tower category $\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)$ of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers], its derived category, and the full subcategory of normalized constructible towers with uniform cohomological and Tor bounds of [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers, def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Let $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ be the derived-complete integral constructible category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], with derived completeness as in [def-weil-derived-complete].

The derived reduction functor
$$r_T=\operatorname{red}_T:D(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E)\longrightarrow D(\operatorname{Tow}(T,\mathcal O_E)),\qquad M\longmapsto(M\otimes^L_{R_T}(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T)_{n\geq1}$$
[det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized] is left adjoint to total derived inverse limit $L_T=R\varprojlim$ (forgetting finite-level scalars to $R_T$ before taking the limit, and using the exact total-derived-limit functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]; [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-limit] fixes the underlying Roos-triangle notation). The unit $M\to L_Tr_TM$ is an isomorphism on derived-complete objects. The counit $r_TL_TC_\bullet\to C_\bullet$ is an isomorphism on normalized towers. For the constructible restriction, assume additionally that $T$ is Noetherian, meaning that it admits a finite affine open cover by spectra of Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. Then the adjunction restricts to mutually inverse equivalences
$$\operatorname{red}_T:\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)\rightleftarrows\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)_{\mathrm{norm}}:R\varprojlim_n.$$

proof.text: Write $\varpi=\varpi_E$ and $B_k=(\mathcal O_E/\varpi^k)_T$. By [lem-weil-l-adic-extension-integers-dvr], $\ell=u\varpi^e$ for a unit $u$ and an integer $e\geq1$: $\ell$ is nonzero and has absolute value strictly less than $1$. Thus $(\ell^n)=(\varpi^{en})$, and the coefficient sheaves in the item are canonically $B_{en}$, with the same quotient maps. The completed sheaf is unchanged: a compatible family on the indices $en$ extends uniquely to index $k$ by projection from any $en\geq k$. Use $\mathscr S(B)$ for the strict varying-coefficient systems of [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension], and put $r(n)=en$, $U=U_r$. The category in the item is $\mathscr S(B_r)$, by the explicit system definition [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers]. Use $\mathcal R_\varpi\dashv\mathcal L_\varpi$ for the actual unbounded derived adjunction of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]. It has $\mathcal L_\varpi=R\lim\circ\operatorname{Res}$, not a categorical inverse limit in a triangulated category. Its reduction is computed from one flat-term K-flat representative $Q$ by $(Q\otimes B_k)_k$, so $U\mathcal R_\varpi=r_T$ with their actual quotient transitions.

source.place: Definitions 3.5.2–3.5.3 and Lemma 3.5.7; explicit ramification reindexing

proof.text: Here is the required derived cofinality argument, on towers over the single fixed ring sheaf $R_T$. Let $V(X)_n=X_{en}$. Its left adjoint is the exact functor $K(Y)_k=Y_{\lceil k/e\rceil}$, with the evident transition maps: a map $K(Y)\to X$ is determined by the maps $Y_n\to X_{en}$, and its other components are obtained by composing with $X_{en}\to X_k$. Exactness is levelwise. Hence $V$ preserves K-injective complexes: for acyclic $A$, a map $A\to VI$ transposes to $KA\to I$, which is null-homotopic since $KA$ is acyclic; the transpose of a null-homotopy is a null-homotopy [def-pur-kinjective-complex]. The functor $n\mapsto en$ on the opposite positive integers is initial: the indices with $en\geq k$ are a nonempty tail, and any two are joined through their maximum. By [lem-weil-pbc-initial-functor-limit], $\lim X\to\lim VX$ is an isomorphism respecting all selected projections. Apply this identity to a K-injective tower resolution. Since its restriction is still K-injective, the total-limit computation in [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit] gives a natural isomorphism $R\lim X\xrightarrow{\sim}R\lim VX$ respecting the selected projections. This argument does not assume exact countable products.

source.place: Tags 0940 (section-derived-limits), 0941 (lemma-derived-limit-is-ok); categories.tex Tag 002R (lemma-initial); derived.tex Tag 070H; explicit subsequence adjoint argument

proof.text: The exact restriction $U:\mathscr S(B)\to\mathscr S(B_r)$ also has an exact right adjoint $J$, given explicitly by $(JC)_k=0$ for $k<e$, and $(JC)_k=\operatorname{Res}_{B_k\to B_{e\lfloor k/e\rfloor}}C_{\lfloor k/e\rfloor}$ for $k\geq e$. Its transitions are restrictions of the transitions of $C$. A system map $D\to JC$ is determined by its components $D_{en}\to C_n$: its $k$th component is $D_k\to D_{e\lfloor k/e\rfloor}\to C_{\lfloor k/e\rfloor}$, and it is zero for $k<e$. This constructs the inverse Hom bijections, including their naturality. Restriction of scalars is exact because it does not change the underlying abelian sheaf; exactness of varying systems is componentwise by [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension]. Consequently $U,J$ preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Applying their termwise unit and counit to complexes and then localizing, using [lem-sf-exact-functor-derived-triangulated], gives $U\dashv J$ on the ordinary unbounded derived categories. The identities descend from the identities on complexes. We have $UJC=C$ strictly. After forgetting to $R_T$, step 2 therefore identifies $\mathcal L_\varpi JC$ with $L_TC$, respecting the level-$n$ projections.

source.place: Adjunction paragraph, expanded at the level of strict derived systems

proof.text:
Combine the two actual adjunctions, rather than taking a limit of degree-zero Hom sets:
$$\operatorname{Hom}(r_TM,C)=\operatorname{Hom}(U\mathcal R_\varpi M,C)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal R_\varpi M,JC)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,\mathcal L_\varpi JC)\cong\operatorname{Hom}(M,L_TC).$$
The first bijection is step 3, the second is [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus], and the last is step 2. They are natural in both variables, so this proves the ambient adjunction. Its unit is the map induced by the strict quotient maps $Q\to Q\otimes B_{en}$: the unit for $U\dashv J$ has identity components at $en$, and the uniformizer adjunction's unit has exactly the quotient components. Thus the resulting coherent map is the canonical derived-completion map. Its counit at level $n$ is the scalar-extension adjoint of $L_TC\to\operatorname{Res}C_n$, by the counit formula in that node and the projection compatibility in step 2. This specifies the natural maps, including their coherence; agreement of unrelated evaluated objects is not being used to choose a system map.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.7(1) and its proof; blueprint Adjunction paragraph

proof.text:
To treat an arbitrary normalized tower $C\in D(\mathscr S(B_r))$, use the existing derived left extension $F=L_rC$ of [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension]. Its formula is
$$F_k=B_k\otimes^L_{B_{e\lceil k/e\rceil}}C_{\lceil k/e\rceil}.$$
In particular $F_{en}=C_n$ and the selected transitions are those of $C$. For adjacent $k+1\to k$, put $a=\lceil k/e\rceil$ and $b=\lceil(k+1)/e\rceil$. The cited node identifies the transition-adjoint with $B_k\otimes^L_{B_{eb}}C_b\to B_k\otimes^L_{B_{ea}}C_a$, induced by $B_{ea}\otimes^L_{B_{eb}}C_b\to C_a$. If $a=b$ this last map is the identity; if $a<b$ it is an isomorphism by normalization of $C$. Thus all adjacent transition-adjoints of $F$ are isomorphisms, and their composites give normalization for every pair of levels, using the same node's tensor-associator compatibility. After forgetting scalars, step 2 gives $\mathcal L_\varpi F\cong L_TC$, with the actual projections to $C_n$ identified. No boundedness or constructibility was used.

source.place: Counit paragraph; explicit interpolation between ell-power levels and uniformizer-power levels

proof.text: The system $F$ of step 5 gives a normalized DVR tower in the precise sense of [def-coef-normalized-dvr-tower]: its underlying strict $R_T$-tower supplies the coherence datum, and the transition-adjoints are the isomorphisms just checked. Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity]. For every $n$ the canonical counit comparison $(\mathcal L_\varpi F)\otimes^L_{R_T}B_{en}\to F_{en}=C_n$ is an isomorphism. Under the projection-preserving isomorphism in step 5 this is exactly the counit component from step 4. The evaluations jointly detect isomorphisms by [lem-pur-system-level-left-extension], so $r_TL_TC\to C$ is an isomorphism of derived systems. This proves the counit clause for all normalized towers, including unbounded ones; finite Tor or constructibility is unnecessary here.

source.place: Lemma 3.5.5 and Lemma 3.5.7(3)–(5); regular principal ideal case

proof.text: For completeness, the unit clause holds even with the triangulated formulation of [def-weil-derived-complete], which does not itself choose the canonical unit. First $\mathcal R_\varpi M$ is normalized for arbitrary $M$: on its flat-term K-flat representative $Q$, [lem-pur-kflat-change-of-rings] makes $Q\otimes B_j$ K-flat over $B_j$, and $(Q\otimes B_j)\otimes_{B_j}B_i=Q\otimes B_i$ for $j\geq i$. Apply [lem-coef-normalized-dvr-effectivity] to this tower. Its counit is invertible. The triangular identity $\mathcal L_\varpi(\epsilon_{\mathcal R_\varpi M})\circ\eta_{\mathcal L_\varpi\mathcal R_\varpi M}=1$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus] makes $\eta_{\mathcal L_\varpi\mathcal R_\varpi M}$ invertible. If $M$ is derived complete, [def-weil-derived-complete] gives a Roos triangle with first object $M$ for its uniformizer reduction tower. The total limit has another such triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. Rotate the two triangles to start with their common $1-s$; (TR3) in [def-weil-triangulated-category] extends the identity on the two product terms to a triangle morphism, whose third map is an isomorphism by [lem-sf-triangle-morphism-iso]. Hence $M\cong\mathcal L_\varpi\mathcal R_\varpi M$ as objects. Writing $H=\mathcal L_\varpi\mathcal R_\varpi$ and choosing the resulting isomorphism $f:M\xrightarrow{\sim}HM$, naturality gives $H(f)\eta_M=\eta_{HM}f$. Both $H(f)$ and $\eta_{HM}f$ are invertible, so $\eta_M=H(f)^{-1}\eta_{HM}f$ is invertible. The cofinality isomorphism of step 2 carries this unit to the ell-power unit of step 4, because both are induced on the same K-flat representative by its strict quotient maps. This proves the asserted canonical unit isomorphism without choosing an arbitrary lift in a Roos triangle.

source.place: Definitions 3.5.2–3.5.3 and Lemma 3.5.7(2); derived.tex axioms TR2–TR3 and two-isomorphism triangle lemma

proof.text: For the constructible restriction now assume that $T$ is Noetherian as in the statement. Let $M\in\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ in the derived-complete integral sense of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed]. Its uniformizer-power reductions are constructible with one cohomological interval. Their finite-torsion constructibility is the condition of [def-weil-finite-torsion-constructibility]. At the selected levels $en$ these are precisely the ell-power reductions. This is literally the intrinsic finite-level constructibility of [def-weil-proetale-constructible-sheaf] required of the levels in [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]: one finite partition of $T$ into locally closed constructible subschemes on each of which the restriction is locally constant with finite stalks. Uniform finite Tor bounds are supplied by [lem-coef-integral-residue-tor]: choose $[a,b]$ containing the cohomology of the uniformizer residue reduction, and every uniformizer reduction has Tor amplitude in that same interval. Apply this to the selected levels $en$. Finally use only the ambient, arbitrary-$M$ clause of the current [det-sp-reduction-tower-normalized]: the reductions form a functorial object of the derived strict-tower category with quotient-induced transitions, and all its reduction maps are isomorphisms. Its separate bounded-constructible integral hypothesis is not needed here. The finite-level constructibility, common cohomological interval and common Tor interval just proved, together with these normalization maps, are exactly [sk-def-sp-normalized-towers]. Hence $r_TM\in\Dctf(T_{\mathrm{proét}},\mathcal O_E/\ell^\bullet)_{\mathrm{norm}}$. The residue-Tor statement permits an arbitrary scheme with $\ell$ invertible; the added Noetherian hypothesis is not used in this forward direction.

source.place: Restriction paragraph, forward direction; explicit uniform Tor hypothesis check

proof.text: Conversely let $C$ be a normalized constructible tower with the common cohomological and Tor bounds in the statement. By [sk-lem-sp-tower], $M=R\varprojlim_nC_n$ lies in $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$. In that statement $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$ is the derived-complete integral category of [def-weil-derived-complete-integral-detailed], its statement dependency: derived complete in the sense of [def-weil-derived-complete], every uniformizer reduction bounded with finite-torsion constructible cohomology, and one cohomological interval for all reductions. This is exactly the category in the item. Both statements use the same completed sheaf $\mathcal O_{E,T}=R_T=\varprojlim_n(\mathcal O_E/\ell^n)_T$ of [sk-def-sp-coefficient-towers] and the same total-limit functor of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit], so $M=L_TC$. Hence $L_T$ sends normalized constructible towers into $\Dbc(T,\mathcal O_E)$. Nothing beyond this statement of the reconstruction lemma is used. The counit on $C$ is the canonical isomorphism of step 6; the reconstruction lemma's level maps are not needed to choose it.

source.place: Restriction: 'R lim sends normalized constructible towers into Dbc(T,O_E) by the reconstruction lemma'

proof.text: By steps 8 and 9, both functors restrict to the stated full subcategories. The natural isomorphisms $\eta_M:M\xrightarrow{\sim}L_Tr_TM$ from step 7 and $\epsilon_C:r_TL_TC\xrightarrow{\sim}C$ from step 6 remain natural on those full subcategories. They give the two composites naturally isomorphic to the identity, with the triangular identities inherited from the ambient adjunction of step 4. These are precisely mutually inverse equivalences, with the functors and natural maps displayed in the statement.
